why: Every ABSOLUTE bound in criteria.json (a millisecond count, a second count)
certifies this runner class as well as this code, so it needs a recorded
number to be derived from. This file is that number: what the lanes actually
measured on a known-good build, so `basis` on each criterion can be checked
RATIO bounds are not listed here and do not need to be — they compare two
halves measured in the same run on the same input, which is why they are
preferred and why two of the four perf lanes have no absolute bound at all.
Re-baselining is its own commit, with its own reason. A bound moved in the
same change that breached it is not a bound.

host.profile: cargo test, debug profile (unoptimized + debuginfo) — the same profile CI runs
host.caveat: A 12-core Windows dev box with a second cargo build competing for the machine. The nightly lane runs on a 2-4 core hosted ubuntu runner, so absolute bounds carry an extra multiple on top of the usual 3x; each criterion's `basis` states its own.

datasets-bulk-upsert.rival_starvation_note: 0 of 504 competing writes starved on an idle box; 2 of 504 (0.4%) on the SAME box minutes later with a competing cargo build running. Real starvation, caused by the machine's spare capacity rather than by the write path — which is why the criterion is a RATE with a 1% ceiling and not a zero count. See the `basis` on rival-starvation-rate.

datasets-duplicate-scan.finding: At Hamming distance 8 the banded index is SLOWER than the all-pairs scan it replaced (1.16x), which the harness has been printing unbounded for its whole life and nobody read. It is not a regression introduced here — it is the first time the number was judged. The d8 bound is set to catch a further blow-up, not to assert a win the design never promised. Worth a separate look at whether the band count should widen with the requested distance.
datasets-duplicate-scan.d20_is_not_a_fair_comparison: At distance 20 the all-pairs reference hits its MAX_DUP_PAIRS cap (10000) almost immediately and stops, so its 89ms is a bail-out and not a scan. The ratio is therefore meaningless at d20 and criteria.json bounds the banded time absolutely instead, and says so.
